keyVerseText: Seven days ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the LORD: on the eighth day shall be an holy convocation unto you; and ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the LORD: it is a solemn assembly; and ye shall do no servile work therein. solemn: Heb. day of restraint
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun עֲצָרָה (ʻătsârâh) derives from the root עָצָר (ʻâtsâr), which carries the core sense of restraining, closing up, or holding back. This root suggests a concept of containment or setting apart, which extends metaphorically to assembling or gathering people within a defined, controlled setting. Beyond the common English gloss of 'assembly,' the root implies a purposeful gathering marked by a form of restraint or solemnity, emphasizing order and sacredness rather than mere crowding.
usageInScripture: The word עֲצָרָה appears 11 times in the Hebrew Bible, predominantly translated as 'a solemn assembly' in various forms. Its usage consistently denotes a sacred or festive gathering, often connected to religious festivals or holy convocations, as shown by the top translations emphasizing solemnity and formal assembly. This reveals that the term is not simply any meeting but one with spiritual and communal significance, underscoring the ordered worship life of Israel.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding עֲצָרָה as a solemn assembly rooted in restraint and sacred gathering enriches our grasp of biblical worship as intentional and reverent. It highlights God's call for His people to come together in holy, ordered fellowship distinct from ordinary activity. This word reminds believers that corporate worship is a divinely appointed time of focused devotion, where distractions and common labors are set aside. In the Christian faith, this points forward to the New Testament call to assemble in Christ's name with reverence and unity, reflecting God’s desire for His people to be spiritually gathered and sanctified.
keyVerseReflection: Leviticus 23:36 commands the Israelites to hold a holy convocation on the eighth day of the festival, explicitly calling it 'a solemn assembly' (עֲצָרָה). This word conveys that this gathering is not casual but marked by a sacred restraint—no servile work is to be done. The term emphasizes the special, set-apart nature of this day, inviting God’s people into focused worship and obedience, which teaches us about the importance of dedicating time exclusively to honoring the LORD.
